questions.question:
Four number-pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 - Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

17 : 82

31 : 158

19 : 92

47 : 232
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: 1st number × 5 - 3 = 2nd number.

Now,

For, 17 : 82

⇒ 17 × 5 - 3 

⇒ 85 - 3 = 82.

For, **31 : 158**

**⇒ 31 × 5 + 3**

**⇒ 155 + 3 = 158.**

For, 19 : 92

⇒ 19 × 5 - 3

⇒ 95 - 3 = 92.

For, 47 : 232

⇒ 47 × 5 - 3

⇒ 235 - 3 = 232.

 

Here, Option 1 **'****31 : 158' is different from the given pairs.**

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

questions.question: If it was Friday on 8 March 1996, then what will be the day of the week on 7 April 2006?
questions.solution:
Given: **8 March 1996 was Friday**.

1996 to 2006 = 10 Years

And, In 10 Years = 2 Leap years and 8 Ordinary Year (because 1996 is counted from 8 March, so 1996 will be treat as ordinary year).

So, 2 Leap Year has 4 odd days,

And, 8 Ordinary Year has 8 odd days.

Total odd days = 4 + 8 = 12.

12 odd days → 12/7 = 1 week and 5 odd days.

then, **8 March 2006 will be Friday + 5 = Wednesday**.

Now, the number of days between 8 March 2006 to 7 April 2006

= 23(March) + 7(April) = 30 days.

= 30 days → 30/7 = 4 week and 2 odd day.

So, **7 April 2006 will be Wednesday + 2 = Friday.**

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which conclusions logically follow/s from the given statements.

**Statements:**

Some aprons are chopsticks.

Some chopsticks are forks.

All forks are knives.

**Conclusion:**

(I): Some chopsticks are aprons.

(II): No forks are knives.
questions.solution:
Given Statements:

Some aprons are chopsticks.

Some chopsticks are forks.

All forks are knives.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/38d5e2bcd392e127e5853894854be0f98f013edfa09b3808b5fd3d2f925abfd0.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some chopsticks are aprons - True (Because, Some aprons are chopsticks also gives Some chopsticks are aprons).

II. No forks are knives - False (Because, All forks are knives).

So, Only conclusion I follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

questions.question:
Three of the following four are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the one that does NOT belong to that group?

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 - Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: (1st number)2 = 2nd number.

Now, checking the options:

**Option 1) 16 - 276 → (16)2 = 256 ≠ 276.**

Option 2) 21 - 441 → (21)2 = 441.

Option 3) 23 - 529 → (23)2 = 529.

Option 4) 19 - 361 → (19)² = 361

So, '16 - 276' is odd among the given options.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

questions.question:
Select the triad from the below options that has the same analogy as the following triads.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 - Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

3 : 26 : 8

7: 342 : 20
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: (1st number)3 - 1 = 2nd number,

1st number **× 3 - 1 = 3rd number.**

Now,

For, 3 : 26 : 8

⇒ (3)3 - 1 = 27 - 1 = 26.

⇒ 3 × 3 - 1 = 9 - 1 = 8.

For, 7: 342 : 20

⇒ (7)3 - 1 = 343 - 1 = 342.

⇒ 7 × 3 - 1 = 21 - 1 = 20.

Similarly, **Option 4) 4 : 63 : 11**

**⇒ (4)3 - 1 = 64 - 1 = 63.**

**⇒ 4 × 3 - 1 = 12 - 1 = 11.**

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question:
In a certain code language,

U @ H means 'U is the son of H',

U % H means 'U is the daughter of H',

U & H means 'U is the mother of H',

U # H means 'U is the father of H'.

If N % M # R @ L & K, then how is N related to K?
questions.solution:
Family Chart:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2a776c0a19b6706031165c847bcb98978a1e150482bd1260c12a74559ea55407.png] 

Decoding the Symbols:

 
 

 Symbol
 @
 %
 &
 #
 
 

 Meaning
 Son
 Daughter
 Mother
 Father
 
 

 

Given: N % M # R @ L & K

It means: N is the Daughter of M, M is the Father of R, R is the Son of L, L is the Mother of K.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d0a033a0d1a71270d6eceefbdf568a2ab436ad41ef94b0d7d3525e4cfc84b1ab.png] 

So, N is the '**Sister**' of K.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
